# CLAIRE Framework Surface Registry

**CORE-OWNED. Adopters do not edit this file.** CLAIRE core upgrades update it
via a clean take-ours merge; an adopter edit here is a misuse the upgrade engine
surfaces as a conflict, never silently overwrites. Your project's own
API / event / DTO / config surfaces live in
[surface-registry.md](surface-registry.md), which references this file.

This document is the source of truth for the **framework-owned** public surfaces:
the `CLAIRE_ORG.md#*-binding` configuration contracts, the neutral-source
schema/manifest, the eject/upgrade/footprint tooling, the cross-skill handoff
contract, the version stamp, the seed-read provenance fields, and the metadata
lifecycle vocabulary. Each carries a backwards-compatibility guarantee for its
documented period (see [Stability Levels](surface-registry.md#stability-levels)).

> **Why this file exists (PI-033 / G-8).** `surface-registry.md` was a
> shared-ownership document: adopter rows and these framework rows shared the same
> Markdown tables, so every core release that added a framework row conflicted
> against the adopter's own row edits under the 3-way merge, with no file-level
> strategy to separate them (the ragpak 3.1.0→3.8.0 field finding). Splitting the
> framework rows here makes core upgrades a clean take-ours and adopter rows a
> clean take-theirs in steady state. The one-time split-transition conflict and
> its resolution are documented in
> [docs/migrations/claire-surfaces-split.md](../migrations/claire-surfaces-split.md).

---

## CLAIRE-development record identifiers

**Read this first if a citation in your tree will not resolve.**

A citation of the form `ADR_CLAIRE-NNNN`, `PROD_CLAIRE-NNN` or `II_CLAIRE-NNN` names a
record in **CLAIRE's own development history** — the decisions, production insights and intent
insights the framework's maintainers wrote while building CLAIRE itself. Those records are
**not distributed to adopting repositories** and are **not expected to resolve in your tree**.

An unresolvable citation of that shape is **documentation residue — expected and benign**. It is
**not an indication that your own tooling failed** to resolve a reference it owns, and it needs no
action from you. You will find such citations in framework-owned files that ship with CLAIRE,
where they serve as provenance for a design decision rather than as a pointer you are meant to
follow.

**Your own records are unaffected.** `ADR-NNN`, `PROD-NNN` and `II-NNN` in your repository are
yours: unchanged, resolving exactly as before, and requiring no rename and no migration on your
side. The `_CLAIRE` suffix exists precisely so that the two namespaces cannot collide — so that
a reference to *our* fourth ADR can never be mistaken for a reference to *yours*. The id allocator
treats the two sets identically in every respect except this one: they are different names.

> **One residual, if you adopted before this release.** CLAIRE's own records only moved into the
> `_CLAIRE` namespace at this release, and exactly one framework file carries our records into your
> tree: `docs/agentic-sdlc/production-insights.md` is copied **whole** at adoption. A repository that
> adopted **before** the re-designation therefore already holds our production-insight entries under
> the bare `PROD-NNN` prefix, and **the upgrade does not rewrite them** — that file is one of the
> handful the upgrade treats as **yours**, so it is deliberately never merged over. That is the right
> default (it is your register, and we do not edit it), but it means the sentence above describes a
> **fresh** adoption exactly, and an older one only after you act.
>
> **Nothing breaks either way, and there is no deadline.** The only consequence is that your own next
> `PROD-NNN` may land on a number one of our entries already used in that file. If you would rather it
> did not: delete our entries from your copy (they are ours, not yours, and nothing in your tree cites
> them), or re-designate their headings to `PROD_CLAIRE-NNN` to match a fresh adoption. Either is a
> one-time edit to a file you own.
>
> The other two prefixes carry no such residual and never did: only `docs/ADR/TEMPLATE.md` is copied
> from our ADR directory, and it mints in **your** grammar; and our `II-NNN` entries are **stripped**
> during adoption, so they never reach your tree at all.

> **Why the suffix, and why only on our side.** Before this split, CLAIRE's own records and an
> adopter's own records shared one identifier grammar. A tool sweeping copied governance content
> could not tell "a citation to a core record this repository never received" from "a citation to
> one of my own records that failed to resolve" — the first is normal, the second is a defect, and
> they were indistinguishable. Core moved rather than asking the fleet to; an adopter's identifiers
> were never the ambiguous half.

## Carve-outs against ADR_CLAIRE-0073 (ratified Decision text)

**Core-development record, recorded here because the count is the point.**
[ADR_CLAIRE-0073](../ADR/0073-a-ratified-adrs-decision-text-is-corrected-by-additive-annotation-never-rewritten-in-place.md)
rules that a ratified ADR's `## Decision` text is preserved byte-for-byte and corrected by an
additive annotation beside it, never rewritten in place. Its scope is narrowed by **two** named
carve-outs, and by nothing else. No third exists; a change that is not squarely inside one of these
two classes is governed by ADR_CLAIRE-0073 unchanged.

| # | Carve-out | Ruled by | The class it removes from ADR_CLAIRE-0073's scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [ADR_CLAIRE-0078](../ADR/0078-a-mechanical-corpus-wide-identifier-re-designation-is-not-a-correction-and-is-carved-out-of-adr-0073-rather-than-superseding-it.md) | BTG-197, ratified at the Maintainer Acceptance gate 2026-09-04 | A **mechanical corpus-wide identifier re-designation**: an identifier token and nothing else moves, every numeric component is preserved, it applies to a whole prefix's corpus at once, and an old-to-new map is published. Four conjunctive terms. |
| 2 | [ADR_CLAIRE-0101](../ADR/0101-a-ratified-decision-clauses-stale-recital-is-restated-in-place-under-a-named-carve-out-never-silently-and-never-by-supersession.md) | BTG-285, ruled by Matt Roberts at the code-review gate 2026-09-16; ratified at the Maintainer Acceptance gate 2026-09-16 | A **stale-recital restatement**: a clause's recited premise has become false while the decision the clause states still holds, only the recital moves, the falsifying change and the surface that owns the fact are both named, the record stays `Accepted`, and its Decision is **not** digest-pinned. Five conjunctive terms. |

**Why this note is in the registry and not only in the two ADRs.** Each carve-out is discoverable
from ADR_CLAIRE-0073 itself -- its `## Status` section carries an additive forward-pointer
annotation for **both**, which is the mechanism that record's own Decision prescribes and the thing
that makes a carve-out an exercise of the rule rather than an override of it. What that gives a
reader is *this record is narrowed, twice*. What this table gives them is the **count and the
classes side by side**, so the next proposal is weighed against **how many came before it** rather
than against whether any did. ADR_CLAIRE-0073 is **not** superseded by either record; its `## Decision`
digest is pinned in `ci-templates/scripts/ratified-decision-digests.txt`, checked by
`ci-templates/scripts/governance-record-gate.sh` on every run, and unchanged since BTG-197 pinned it.

**Not a registered surface, and no row shape was invented for it.** `docs/ADR/` records are
core-development history (see the section above), carry no adopter-facing guarantee period, and
neither ADR_CLAIRE-0073 nor ADR_CLAIRE-0078 has ever had a row in the tables below. This is a
narrative note on the footing of the *OpenCode-adapter harness known-red set* section further down:
a cross-cutting fact a reader of this registry needs, recorded against the ticket that established
it.

Triage allocates ids; elicit enforces all-or-nothing. **PI-024 (F3): NON-FUNCTIONAL on OpenCode.** This handoff is command→command composition (RC-3). OpenCode has no command→command primitive and no neutral field names the delegation target, so the OpenCode adapter grants the `task` delegation capability but does **not** wire this handoff — `/claire-elicit` and `/claire-triage` compile on OpenCode but their composition does not run. RC-3 (and this surface) remain **fully functional on the reference runtime** (Claude Code reference). Functional wiring on OpenCode is deferred to a follow-up (PI-024 DEC-013: a neutral delegation-target field). **BTG-277: a SECOND and INDEPENDENT OpenCode exposure on this same skill -- not the RC-3 gap above.** BTG-277 moves `/claire-elicit`'s probe menu onto the runtime's **native question control** (Claude Code `AskUserQuestion`; OpenCode's built-in `question`). The Claude Code limb was **measured** -- probe P-A rendered 705 characters in a per-option `description` with no truncation, ellipsis or reflow. The **OpenCode limb was never measured**, and two risks ship undischarged there: (1) the emitted **deny-by-default** `permission:` map may refuse the control outright, leaving probe presentation **non-functional** -- and that is a **REGRESSION this change introduces**, because the prior printed menu required no tool at all and prose cannot be denied; (2) an **undocumented** per-option `description` ceiling could truncate a candidate on screen while the full text is recorded, so the operator selects from text they could not fully see and `problem.md` records a faithful transcription of an uninformed choice, with no error and no signal. **No CI gate, harness or telemetry in this repository detects either** -- a green suite is evidence about what the neutral source *directs*, never about what a runtime *does*. The only detector is **a human running `/claire-elicit` on OpenCode**, which is also the discharge point for both. Accepted knowingly at the BTG-277 maintainer gate on the stated basis that no adopter runs `/claire-elicit` on OpenCode today; recorded **here** rather than only in `archive/BTG-277/` so an OpenCode adopter meets it where the RC-3 gap already sits. |
| `follow-up filing composition contract v1` | `/claire-review` step 6, `/claire-maintain` step 6b, `/claire-archive` step 2e -> `/claire-triage --file-only` | **BTG-345 NOTE — the callers below are migrated to the draft-path form.** The inline free-text description on `/claire-triage --file-only` sunsets 2026-10-14 (see the Deprecation Log row below and `docs/migrations/triage-file-only-draft-path.md`). BTG-281 introduced the draft-path replacement but deferred migrating these three callers; BTG-345 completes that migration — each gate now writes the confirmed candidate's description verbatim to `specs/drafts/<ticket-id>-<gate>-<UTC>-<N>.md` (deleted after a zero-exit filing, kept as evidence after a non-zero exit, and kept on the degraded path) before composing. `<UTC>` is read once per gate run and shared by that run's candidates, so a later run of the same gate never overwrites an earlier run's kept draft (BTG-345 DEC-014, code-review cycle 1 fix). BTG-281's F0 clause still changes the outcome of a **mangled** composed call from "files a ticket about a stray word" to a loud halt with no id allocated, which is a strictly safer behavior change on this contract. Call: `/claire-triage --file-only <draft-path>`, once per human-confirmed candidate. Record: `submission.md` `## Resolution` -> `Follow-ups created`, carrying exactly one disposition per candidate -- **Filed** (id, description, filing phase, date, `specs/<id>/`), **Duplicate of \<id>** (no id allocated), **Folded into \<id>** (recorded only once the target's write lands), **None owed**, **Declined** (count, phase, reason each), or **Deferred** (cause + pointer to `## Discussion`); Filed, Duplicate, Folded, Declined and Deferred may combine, None owed stands alone, and the field is never empty and never a bare none-shaped token | Beta | 1 release cycle | The framework's second cross-skill coordination contract, and the first that a human gate confirms per item (BTG-208). The three commands gain `command-composition`; the `claire-maintainer`, `claire-archivist` and `claire-reviewer` ROLES deliberately do not -- a delegated role cannot issue the confirmation menu and would halt, so a role grant would ship a capability that halts (BTG-208 DEC-002). Per-tier filing point is stated in `docs/policies/change-tiers.md`: Low -> `/claire-review` (its only human gate), Medium/High -> review then maintain then archive in that order, Trivial -> no governed phase raises a candidate at all (`Agents: No`), so coverage there is `/claire-archive` alone and only for a release cut. **NON-FUNCTIONAL ON OPENCODE, by the same RC-3 gap the `elicit->triage` row above records:** the adapter grants the `task` delegation capability but wires no command->command composition, so a composing step emits but does not compose. Unlike that row, this contract DEFINES the behaviour for that case rather than leaving it undefined -- where the host runtime cannot compose, **or** no human is present to confirm, the step files nothing, allocates nothing, never simulates the callee, emits a named notice (`followup.filing.composition_unavailable` / `followup.filing.confirmation_channel_unavailable`), and records each candidate plus its exact runnable filing command. Fully functional on the reference runtime. Shape enforced by the BDD harness `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-208-followup-disposition.test.sh`: a hard verdict over live `specs/` -- every in-scope record is conformance-checked against the four dispositions, and a non-conforming one fails the harness by name -- and **report-only** over `archive/` (the 21 already-dangling archived records are out of scope and are never rewritten). The harness is discovered by the harness-sweep glob and earns **no row in the composed gate runner**, so it sits outside that composed verdict (BTG-208 DEC-011, whose severity claim DEC-012 corrects). **It is framework-development material and does NOT ship to adopters**: `artifacts/footprint.generated` classes `ci-templates` as `kind=framework_dev`, and `adopt-claire.sh`'s `COPY_PATHS` carries no path under `ci-templates/scripts/tests/`. So in an adopting repo this contract is enforced by the three commands' own steps and by the human gates that confirm each candidate -- never by a shipped check -- and no CI wiring of the adopter's could run this harness, because the adopter does not have it. In core it is enforced by a manual invocation or by the end-of-pass baseline sweep, which is the same net the other 165 harnesses sit in. The grant is also **coarse**: RC-2 `command-composition` is not callee-scoped, so the three commands can compose any skill; the narrowing to `/claire-triage --file-only` is stated in their bodies, not enforced by the vocabulary. **BTG-343 NOTE** -- the enumeration narrows further: only entries classed `out-of-scope-defect` are ever candidates (the other four classes -- `adr-owed`, `nit`, `hygiene`, `observation` -- are logged, never presented); each candidate is checked against open and archived prior work and carries a `new` / `duplicate of <id>` / `fold into <id>` verdict before presentation; the Record gains `Duplicate of <id>` and `Folded into <id>` forms and a per-class tally clause; and `adr-owed` is routed exclusively to a new `/claire-archive` step 1b. `Call:` was unchanged **by BTG-343**; BTG-345 moved it to the draft-path form (see the BTG-345 NOTE above). See `docs/policies/finding-classes.md`. |

A resolved value of `0` is **valid** and records a real `0m` stage (BTG-112 AC-5); per **DEC-010** that is reachable **only** through this override and never as a shipped §12 default. **Source of record (NOT duplicated here):** the resolution is implemented ONCE, in `ci-templates/scripts/stage-effort.sh`, and the rule is stated ONCE in `CLAIRE_ORG.md` §12 (*Per-operator override*). This row summarises and points back; it is deliberately not a second source of truth for the values, which §12 alone owns. |

| `CLAIRE_WORKLOG_FACTOR_TRIAGE` | Environment variable (numeric, per-user) | `ci-templates/scripts/worklog-split.sh`, the single split computation site both tracker adapters invoke in split mode (BTG-315 DEC-003), via `/claire-sync-jira` and `/claire-sync-youtrack` | **Absent ⇒ the `CLAIRE_ORG.md` §19 table value for `triage`.** No value is embedded here or in the script; §19 is read live | Beta | 1 release cycle | The factor is the **operator's** share of each projected `stage_effort` entry: `1` sends the whole entry to the operator, `0` sends it to the §9 agent-time user. Resolution rule: present **and** matching `^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?\|\.[0-9]+)$` (whole numbers, decimals and the leading-dot form such as `.5`), with **at most 9** fractional digits once trailing fractional zeros are stripped, and a value in the closed interval `[0, 1]` ⇒ used in place of the §19 table value **for that stage only**; absent, empty, trailing-dot (`1.`), signed, suffixed, whitespace-padded, out of range, or over-precise ⇒ **quietly ignored** (BTG-112 DEC-003 parity; BTG-315 OQ-7, OQ-8). The name is **derived mechanically** from the stage id, uppercased with `-` mapped to `_`, the same rule as the `CLAIRE_STAGE_EFFORT_MULTIPLIER_*` family. **POLARITY CONTRAST:** the override VALUE is quiet-ignore, but an unusable §19 value (no §19 section, no row for the stage, an unknown stage id, or a value failing the same grammar) resolves to `1` (all operator) and emits the non-halting warning `worklogsplit.factor.org_value_unusable stage=<id> cause=<missing\|invalid>`, which never carries the value: a missing binding is louder than a missing preference (Behavior 5; BTG-315 OQ-7). Consulted **only** in split mode (a §9 per-prefix row naming a non-empty agent-time user), so an unconfigured adopter's projection never reads it and never sees the warning. The resolved factor is never printed and never written to a worklog. **Source of record (NOT duplicated here):** implemented once in `worklog-split.sh`; the rule is stated once in `CLAIRE_ORG.md` §19. The accept pattern in this row is diffed against the script by BTG-315 S-1.10. |

Consulted **only** in split mode (a §9 per-prefix row naming a non-empty agent-time user), so an unconfigured adopter's projection never reads it and never sees the warning. The resolved factor is never printed and never written to a worklog. **Source of record (NOT duplicated here):** implemented once in `worklog-split.sh`; the rule is stated once in `CLAIRE_ORG.md` §19. The accept pattern in this row is diffed against the script by BTG-315 S-1.10. |
| `CLAIRE_ORG.md#actual-effort-accumulation` (section 12) | Markdown section / config slot | Every adopting repo (substituted in their own CLAIRE_ORG.md fork); `ci-templates/scripts/stage-effort.sh`, which parses this section's per-stage multiplier table out of `ORG_FILE` at run time; the six `CLAIRE_STAGE_EFFORT_MULTIPLIER_*` rows above, each of which already resolved its absent-default to this section | the per-stage review-multiplier table + the rounding rule (round UP to the next 15-minute increment, minimum `15m` for any non-zero computed time) + the single-source-of-truth rule that forbids restating a multiplier value anywhere else | Beta | 1 release cycle | Added by **BTG-275** under **Gate 1's OQ-1 ruling**, as amended by BTG-275 DEC-016, which adopted the class predicate: *an `CLAIRE_ORG.md` section is a registered surface iff it is a per-adopter-substituted contract that at least one CLAIRE tool or role resolves AS A VALUE, **and** is declared as a contract rather than as a practice.* Section 12 satisfies **both** limbs -- `stage-effort.sh` resolves its table as a value, and it is a contract an adopter substitutes, not a practice record. The registry no longer holds six rows deferring to an authority it does not list. The predicate is a CLASS ruling, not an instance one: every section it excludes carries a row in *Ruled not registered* below. |
| `CLAIRE_ORG.md#worklog-attribution-split` (section 19) | Markdown section / config slot | Every adopting repo (substituted in their own CLAIRE_ORG.md fork); `ci-templates/scripts/worklog-split.sh`, which parses this section's per-stage table out of `ORG_FILE` at run time, section-scoped on the section heading and never by a file-wide grep; the six `CLAIRE_WORKLOG_FACTOR_*` rows above, each of which resolves its absent-default to this section | the per-stage operator-share factor table (one row per `stage_effort.stage`; factor in `[0, 1]` under the accept grammar of the `CLAIRE_WORKLOG_FACTOR_*` rows) + the split rule (the agent leg is the entry times one minus the factor, floored to a 15-minute increment; the operator leg takes the remainder, so the legs always sum to the entry and any off-boundary remainder lands on the operator) + the single-source-of-truth rule forbidding any restatement of a factor value | Beta | 1 release cycle | Added by **BTG-315** under Gate 1's OQ-1 ruling: a new section after §18 in `CLAIRE_ORG.md`, appended unnumbered in `CLAIRE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md`; the template ships the same initial values as this repository (OQ-2). Satisfies both limbs of the BTG-275 DEC-016 class predicate: `worklog-split.sh` resolves its table as a value, and it is a contract an adopter substitutes. **Inert** until an agent-time user is configured on a §9 per-prefix row. Projection-only: the §12 ledger (`stage_effort` / `actual_effort`) is unaffected and remains the sole record of effort. **POLARITY:** a missing section, a missing row or an invalid value resolves to `1` (all operator) with the non-halting `worklogsplit.factor.org_value_unusable` warning, never a halt (OQ-7). A value change is Trivial tier; a stage-key or column-type change is a shape change. |

| `artifacts/SCHEMA.md` (neutral-source artifact schema) | Schema / config contract | Stable | 2 release cycles | Every adopting repo's authoring; the update/override (Workstream A), eject (Workstream B), and OpenCode-adapter workstreams. RC-1 role fields + RC-2 command fields, capability vocabulary only, no concrete runtime primitive. Introduced by PI-012 (ratifies ADR_CLAIRE-0008 clause 3). The runtime-neutral source of record for roles and commands; the round-trip contract pins it. Per-runtime adapters compile it to native layouts. **PI-023 (additive, non-breaking):** the RC-2 `sidecar_script` field prose is clarified — it names the **entry-point** script, and when present the adapter copies the **entire** colocated `artifacts/commands/<name>/` directory verbatim into the compiled skill (was: a single file). The field name, grammar (relative filename), and required/optional status are **unchanged**; existing single-file sidecars compile byte-identically (DEC-002/005). An additive refinement of ADR_CLAIRE-0008 clause 3 (DEC-006), no new ADR. **PI-024 (additive, non-breaking):** the Body placeholder vocabulary gains **four** placeholders — `{{artifact_path:<tree>:<name>}}` (an artifact's primary file), `{{sidecar:<command>:<relpath>}}` (a colocated sidecar file), `{{artifact_glob:<tree>}}` (a role/command file glob, e.g. `.claude/agents/*/AGENT.md` vs `.opencode/agents/*.md`), and `{{runtime_root}}` (the bare runtime tree root `.claude` vs `.opencode`) — closing the DEC-010 path-tail gap for both `.md` bodies AND sidecar `.sh` scripts (sidecars are now expanded per-runtime at emit, not raw-copied; F2). bump-model is **fully neutralized** via `{{artifact_glob}}` with **no exception** (F6: OpenCode also uses `model:` frontmatter, so the earlier frontmatter-coupling exception is withdrawn). Existing `{{artifact_root:<tree>}}` is unchanged. **BTG-022 (additive, non-breaking):** the Body placeholder vocabulary gains two rows documenting already-shipped adapter behavior — `{{artifact_root:hooks}}` (→ `.claude/claire-hooks`, `n/a (Claude-only)` on OpenCode) and `{{settings_file}}` (→ `.claude/settings.json`, `n/a (Claude-only)`). Both were live in the claude-code adapter since BTG-008 but unregistered (II-009 drift); registered here across all three representations (`NEUTRAL_SANCTIONED_PATTERNS`, this table, the adapter expanders). No existing placeholder changes. **BTG-023 (additive, non-breaking):** the two "Expands to (OpenCode)" cells for `{{artifact_root:hooks}}` and `{{settings_file}}` are reconciled from the literal `n/a (Claude-only)` to the now-accurate expansion the OpenCode adapter produces — `.claude/claire-hooks` / `.claude/settings.json` — with the preserved "(Claude-only; borrows the Claude value — no OpenCode binding; hooks tree not emitted, BTG-023)" annotation (OQ-1). Hooks stay a Claude-only capability (BTG-022 OQ-2 / DEC-003 unchanged); this is an honest clarification of the column header, introducing **no** `.opencode/...` vocabulary and no new placeholder token. **BTG-042 (additive, non-breaking):** two prose reconciliations, no field/grammar change (DEC-003 option b). (1) The RC-2 `sidecar_script` field prose now states the value names any **one** colocated entry file — a script **or** a content/markdown template — with two roles (copy-trigger switch + single entry-point existence gate), and that the adapter copies the entire colocated directory verbatim and **kind-agnostically** (every file rides along regardless of kind, not just the named one). (2) The "one file per artifact" framing is clarified to refer to the **primary** role/command `.md`; the optional sidecar directory is a separate multi-file kind-agnostic concern. The field **name, grammar, and required/optional status are unchanged**; existing sidecars compile byte-identically. Companion schema-tightening (build tooling, not this surface): `compile-schema.sh --check-schema` now fails closed on a duplicate frontmatter key (IMPOSSIBLE_STATE `schema.validate.duplicate_frontmatter_key`), rejecting only already-invalid artifacts that had a silently-dropped value. A doc-only refinement; no new ADR. **BTG-134 (additive, non-breaking):** the RC-2 command block gains an **optional** `capability_tier: Deep-reasoning | Fast-mechanical` field -- the same ADR_CLAIRE-0005 neutral vocabulary the RC-1 role field already uses, and no concrete model identifier is added. It is **optional for a command** and stays **required for a role**: `compile-schema.sh`'s command required-field list (`name description arguments allowed_tool_capabilities`) is **unchanged**, so every existing command remains valid and compiles byte-identically. When declared, the tier resolves through the adapter's existing `*_tier_model` -- no new mapping table -- and the compiled command carries a `model:` line whose value is that adapter's own string (unprefixed on the Claude mirror, provider-prefixed on the OpenCode one). Declaring the key with an empty or absent value is refused by `--check-schema` (IMPOSSIBLE_STATE `schema.validate.command_tier_empty`); an unmapped value fails the compile (`compile.output.missing_artifact`). A runtime whose command format has no model slot emits nothing and does not fail. Additive under ADR_CLAIRE-0008 clause 3; no new ADR. |

Hard verdict over active `specs/`, report-only over `archive/` (the no-backfill hard line); the gate is read-only and carries **no** multiplier value (single-source-of-truth preserved, DEC-005). The script path and row label (`effort-boundary`) are unchanged to avoid a rename break; the broadened remit is documented here. The row is appended **only on the first (non-re-entrant) entry**, guarded by a `CLAIRE_GATES_RUNNING` sentinel the runner exports and checks: the harness's own `R-1` scenario invokes `run-gates.sh`, so a nested run **omits** the harness row to bound the recursion (the `gate.reentry.unbounded` seam). The harness path resolves from `OPENCODE_ADAPTER_HARNESS` (env-overridable, real path default) so gate-wiring tests can point the row at a pass/fail stub. No fail-fast change; the four prior baseline-red scenarios (S-7.2/S-3.3/S-10.1/S-10.3) are reconciled by assertion-correction, so the harness is uniformly green before it gates. The estimate gate keeps its filename (keep-one-name, DEC-003 — no referenced path disappears); the second gate script is added to the preflight loop. Additive, no fail-fast change; the union of emitted seams is byte-unchanged (AC-2). It carries two plain-text data contracts alongside it: `dead-citation-exemptions.txt`, a permanent **allowlist** that fails closed and may grow only with a recorded reason, and `dead-citation-baseline.txt`, a SHA-stamped **debt** ledger that may only SHRINK -- an added baseline entry fails the gate (`citation.baseline.grew`), or the ratchet would be decorative. Two files rather than one because a design exemption and a debt entry have opposite lifecycles (DEC-004). The same script serves `/claire-archive` in `--id` mode: one classifier, two callers. Adopters copying `ci-templates/` generate their own baseline with `--emit-baseline`; an adopter with no dead citations gets an empty one. No existing row, argument, or exit-code contract changes. **BTG-340 (additive, non-breaking):** `dead-citation-ledgers.sh`'s `pattern_matches()`/`is_exempt()` gains a FOURTH exemption-pattern form, `<path>:<line>` or `<path>:<line1>-<line2>`, matching ONLY the named line(s) of the named file instead of the whole file -- documented in `dead-citation-exemptions.txt`'s own FORMAT section and threaded through every `is_exempt` call site in `dead-citation-gate.sh` (`decisions.md` DEC-076, DEC-084). The three existing pattern forms (exact path, `dir/`, `prefix**`) are unchanged and continue to match byte-identically; no existing row, argument, or exit-code contract changes. **BTG-100 (additive, non-breaking bug fix):** adds one blocking row `copy-paths-reconcile` (`ci-templates/scripts/copy-paths-reconcile-gate.sh` + its committed `copy-paths-reconcile-ledger.txt`), asserting that every `claire-adopt` `COPY_PATHS` entry is reachable by an ALREADY-ADOPTED repo or is recorded as a deliberate, reasoned exception. An adopter's `artifacts/footprint.generated` is a point-in-time snapshot of `COPY_PATHS` frozen at adopt time (ADR_CLAIRE-0009), and `ci-templates/scripts` is not a `tree_root`, so an entry added after that snapshot is invisible to that adopter forever unless `upgrade-collect.sh`'s `RECONCILE` table names it (PROD_CLAIRE-010; BTG-083 added three entries and zero rows). The rule is TOTAL coverage, deliberately NOT release-relative -- a descriptor freezes at adopt time and can predate any release, so a release-relative test leaves exactly the affected population uncovered. ADOPTER-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated plainly and precisely: an adopter who has copied `run-gates.sh` in **together with the gate script** and who then adds a `COPY_PATHS` entry will see a NEW FAILING ROW until they add a `RECONCILE` row or a reasoned ledger row. An adopter who copied `run-gates.sh` **without** the gate script sees something different and louder: the runner's pre-existing missing-gate preflight aborts the whole run with `exit 2` before ANY gate is reported -- not a failing row. Both are in-contract for a Beta surface, but they are not the same outcome and the earlier wording of this clause conflated them (BTG-100 maintainer gate). That is additive-but-stricter, which is in-contract for a Beta surface. A reason-less or stale ledger row FAILS here, deliberately unlike the sibling `dead-citation` row's WARN -- a human requester ruling at BTG-100's Spec Approval gate (`decisions.md` DEC-011), restated in the gate script's own header so it does not read as drift. No existing row is removed, renamed, or reordered; no argument or exit-code contract changes. The gate itself is deliberately NOT separately registered and NOT added to `COPY_PATHS` -- it checks framework-dev tables adopters neither hold nor edit, and adding it to `COPY_PATHS` would trip its own check. **BTG-097 (additive, non-breaking):** adds a `sync-jira-server-live-verification` row (`sync-jira-server-live-verification-gate.sh`) -- the standing structural gate for `CLAIRE_ORG.md` §16, asserting that every commit since §16 landed which touches the `/claire-sync-jira` **neutral source** belongs to a ticket whose `test-plan.md` declares the live verification naming the target project §16 designates, and whose `submission.md`, once archived, records the observed values **and** a disposition. Read-only; needs none of §16's parameters (no credential, no network, no project key). It ships one plain-text data contract, `sync-jira-server-live-verification-ledger.txt`, a fail-closed attribution/exemption ledger: `attribute` rows key on a 40-hex sha, `exempt` rows key on a **ticket id** (this repo squash-merges, so a branch sha does not survive the merge) and must cite the `DEC-` that granted them; an `exempt` row discharges **both** §16 halves. The gate is internal to this runner (not a separately-consumed surface), mirroring the `compose`/`sidecar-completeness`/`dead-citation` rows, and reaches no adopter (absent from `adopt-claire.sh`'s `COPY_PATHS`); a tree whose `CLAIRE_ORG.md` has no §16 gets a loud `NOT APPLICABLE` and exit 0. No existing row, argument, or exit-code contract changes. **BTG-109:** no new row -- the existing `copy-paths-reconcile` row's gate gains a **fourth required input**, `ci-templates/scripts/copy-paths-debt-baseline.txt`, the owed-debt record that ADR_CLAIRE-0033's lifecycle split moved out of the findings ledger. It joins the gate's existing refuse-before-reporting pre-flight, so its absence exits 2 naming it (deliberately: a record of a deliberate fail-open must not be deletable into a green verdict). Two assertions are added inside that same gate -- the debt baseline holds zero rows (`SEAM_VIOLATION upgrade.reconcile.debt_baseline_nonempty`) and the findings ledger's declared `# Entries:` count matches its actual row count (`SEAM_VIOLATION upgrade.reconcile.findings_ledger_grew`); a ledger with no declared count declares nothing and is not asserted against, so no older ledger is retroactively failed. Positive structural requirements on a separate file, never a denylist content classifier over the findings prose (ADR_CLAIRE-0041). The gate stays `find`-free and `python3`-free and performs no traversal. The new input is framework-repo-internal -- absent from `adopt-claire.sh`'s `COPY_PATHS` and from every `RECONCILE` row, exactly like the gate and ledger beside it -- so it reaches no adopter; an adopter who copied `ci-templates/` wholesale carries it, and a selective copy gets a loud named setup failure rather than a wrong verdict. No existing row, argument or exit-code contract changes. **BTG-136 (additive, non-breaking; the runner's own behaviour is unchanged):** records the CALLER-SIDE half of this row's re-entrancy contract. `run-gates.sh` itself is untouched -- its behaviour, its variables, its announcement text and its exit contract are byte-identical, and an adopter who never sets `CLAIRE_GATES_RUNNING` sees no difference. What is new is an obligation on the CALLERS: every harness that invokes the real runner declares what it wants from the appended `opencode-adapter` row, in one of three ways -- GUARD (an inline `CLAIRE_GATES_RUNNING=<tag>` prefix at the call, which omits the row and announces the omission), STUB (an inline `OPENCODE_ADAPTER_HARNESS=<stub>` redirect, which keeps the row present at near-zero cost), or ACCEPT (no change, plus an exemption marker at the site citing a decision entry that authorises that file BY NAME, ADR_CLAIRE-0056). Nine previously-undeclared invocations across seven harnesses (`btg-023-opencode-hooks-parity` x3, `btg-052-effort-format`, `btg-100-copy-paths-backfill`, `compile-overlay`, `hooks-regression`, `pi-046-tiermap-sweep`, `sidecar-completeness-gate`) now GUARD, and each asserts the `[opencode-adapter] SKIPPED (re-entrant sentinel set: ...)` line its own tag causes -- so a dropped prefix fails a test rather than silently restoring the cost. Two harnesses are NAMED EXCEPTIONS rather than dispositions, because the sentinel's own state is what they test: `ci-templates/scripts/tests/opencode-adapter.test.sh` (its forced-unset run is the corpus's only assertion that the WHOLE composed verdict including `[opencode-adapter] PASS` is green -- the coverage that makes the nine guards safe rather than merely cheaper) and `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-077-compile-cache.test.sh` (it parameterizes the sentinel across scenarios, one of them deliberately empty). Each carries a comment-only marker at its site citing the decision entry that authorises it. | `ci-templates/scripts/baseline-diff.sh` (branch-versus-baseline harness sweep) | CLI / CI tooling | Beta | 1 release cycle | Contributors and delegated agents running the end-of-pass baseline regression diff; adopter repos that copy `ci-templates/`. Glob-discovers `ci-templates/scripts/tests/*.test.sh` independently on the branch tree and a baseline tree and sweeps the **union** (PI-025 discovery; an empty glob on either tree is a loud FATAL before any harness runs). The tree under test is **never swept in place**: a disposable copy is made and the copy is swept, so a harness -- which runs with its working directory set to that tree -- cannot damage the original (`--in-place` opts out, loudly, and is not the default). The baseline ref is resolved from `CLAIRE_ORG.md#branch-strategy-binding` (`integration-branch`), never hardcoded -- an absent, empty or un-substituted binding HALTs naming it; by default a detached `git worktree` is created at that ref in an out-of-repo-tree scratch dir and removed on every exit path, while a `--baseline <path>` tree is adopted, verified clean AND at the expected ref (HALT naming both commits otherwise), and never removed. Runs items with **no fail-fast** (sequentially until BTG-138; bounded-concurrently since -- see the BTG-138 clause below), each as an isolated `bash` subprocess (never sourced) bounded by a per-harness timeout (`--timeout` / `BASELINE_DIFF_TIMEOUT`, default 600s; an unavailable timeout facility is announced, never silently unbounded, and a bound the facility itself rejects HALTs before the sweep rather than reporting every item as could-not-run). Classifies each harness GREEN / NEW-RED / PRE-RED / FIXED / ADDED / REMOVED / TIMEOUT / ERROR; **exit 0 iff** the sweep completed on both trees **and** no harness is NEW-RED, TIMEOUT or ERROR (PRE-RED, FIXED, ADDED-green and REMOVED are reported and do not fail the verdict; an incomplete sweep never exits 0). Leading- and trailing-edge `[i/N]` progress plus all seams on **stderr**, report and verdict on **stdout** (the verdict is the last stdout line); output shape is TTY-independent -- no ANSI, no carriage-return redraw, never suppressed off a terminal. Per-item logs and the run report are written outside both trees; **zero** files are written inside either tree. Never sets, exports, unsets or edits `CLAIRE_GATES_RUNNING` and HALTs if it is already set on entry (BTG-054 interoperation); `run-gates.sh` and `.builds/compile-gate.yml` receive zero edits. Introduced by BTG-078 (decisions.md DEC-001: a peer of `run-gates.sh`, not a row inside it -- a row carries one exit code and this sweep's output is a three-way per-harness classification). Pinned by `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-078-baseline-diff.test.sh` (glob-discovered, fixture-driven; it never invokes the runner against the real repository tree). **A GREEN classification is only ever reported for an item whose harness actually executed: a facility, filesystem or working-directory failure that yields an exit code WITHOUT running the harness is ERROR, never folded into a pass-versus-fail comparison (decisions.md DEC-027) -- "every item completed" above means "every item ran", not merely "an exit code came back".** **BTG-135 (additive-but-stricter, in-contract for Beta):** the classification gains a **scenario-level** fold, computed from the per-item logs the sweep already writes -- **no additional execution**. Scenario ids are the first whitespace-delimited token after the `PASS` / `FAIL` markers each harness prints, which makes that long-implicit 120/120 harness output convention explicitly load-bearing; a harness that ran to completion but yields zero scenario lines emits `LINEAGE_GAP baseline.scenario.unparseable` rather than being read as regression-free, and a duplicated id folds FAIL-wins. Each id folds `(branch, baseline)` the same way harnesses do, and only harnesses that produced a PASS or FAIL verdict on **both** trees are folded (an item that could not be RUN carries no comparable information; a harness present on one tree only is already announced by its own ADDED / REMOVED row). New report rows carry a distinct `SCEN-` prefix and a `scenarios:` counts line; existing rows, arguments, the exit-code vocabulary and the verdict-line grammar are unchanged, and the verdict remains the last stdout line. **Behaviour change, stated plainly:** the verdict now ALSO fails on `SCEN-NEW-RED` -- a scenario PASS on the baseline tree and FAIL on the branch tree -- which can arise only inside a harness that is FAIL on the branch, so the blast radius is exactly the II-069 gap a harness-level verdict structurally cannot see. `SCEN-REMOVED` is announced (`SEAM_VIOLATION baseline.scenario.removed_on_branch`) and does **not** fail the verdict, mirroring the harness-level REMOVED rule; `SCEN-NEW-RED` also emits `IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.scenario.new_red`. Fixture-pinned by the same harness (`btg-078-baseline-diff.test.sh` S-2.1..S-2.8, C-1, C-2). **BTG-138 (additive control; one modified behaviour, stated plainly):** the sweep runs **bounded-concurrently**, not sequentially. `--workers <n>` / `BASELINE_DIFF_WORKERS` sets the number of harnesses in flight; the default is `max(2, min(8, nproc/2))`, announced on a header line naming the observed core count, with an announced fallback of 4 when `nproc` is unavailable, and a value that is not an integer >= 1 HALTs before the sweep (`IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.workers.unusable_bound`, exit 2). A value above the observed core count is accepted with a warning, never refused. `--workers 1` reproduces the sequential **execution** contract exactly and is the supported one-flag bisect for a suspected concurrency artifact. Arguments, the exit-code vocabulary, the classification, the stdout **report grammar** and the verdict-as-last-line are all **unchanged**, and the report stays byte-stable across runs because it iterates the sorted union rather than completion order. **Changed, on stderr only:** every progress line is printed by the parent and carries a **worker token** (`w3`); the bracketed counter is a **dispatch** ordinal on a `RUNNING` line and a **completion** ordinal on a verdict line, so an item's two lines correlate by identity rather than by that counter; and a new `baseline-diff: in flight N/W: ...` **digest line** names every in-flight item with its elapsed-so-far, on each completion and on a 30 s heartbeat (settable by `BASELINE_DIFF_HEARTBEAT_MS`, an internal tunable), bounding the maximum dark interval at the heartbeat rather than at one harness. A consumer parsing progress **bytes** must adjust; nothing is removed, so this is recorded rather than deprecated. Each dispatched item publishes an atomically-renamed two-line result record (`verdict=`, `elapsed_ms=`) outside both trees; a missing, torn or ungrammatical record is `ERROR` (`baseline.result.missing` / `baseline.result.corrupt`), **never a silently absent key** -- an absent key reads as "harness not present on that tree" and folds to `ADDED`, i.e. exit 0 over an item that never ran. A worker's exit status is never the verdict. The runner additionally fingerprints each tree before and after the sweep (method pinned per tree at the start) and fails the verdict on a difference (`baseline.tree.mutated_during_sweep`, the `CONTAMINATED` term), which makes this row's existing "zero files are written inside either tree" claim checkable about the **sweep as a whole** rather than about the runner alone; when neither a version-control status nor a hashing walk is available the backstop is announced as unavailable (`SEAM_VIOLATION baseline.tree.immutability_guard_unavailable`) and the sweep proceeds. The corpus-side invariant is pinned by `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-138-tree-immutability.test.sh` (glob-derived; zero **unexempted** write-into-tree sites, every declared survivor listed on every run) and the runner-side behaviour by `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-138-concurrency.test.sh`. `run-gates.sh` receives **zero edits**: AC-5's verification found no gap, because a process environment is copied at fork and is never shared memory. **Isolation, added at the cycle-3 gate after measurement (decisions.md DEC-021):** concurrency alone was not deterministic -- two W=8 sweeps over the same tree pair disagreed -- because in-flight items shared one repository tree and one temp directory. Two guarantees now hold and are stated as contract. First, a harness that **declares** a write into the tree it runs in (the tree-write exemption markers the immutability guard above already requires) is dispatched **ALONE**: the pool is drained to zero before it starts and nothing is dispatched while it runs, so no concurrent item can observe its plant. The set is glob-derived from those markers -- never a roster -- matched by basename and unioned across both trees, its census is announced on stderr on **every** run (`baseline-diff: solo set = ...`), and each solo dispatch announces itself; the cost is that those harnesses are serialized. A baseline tree predating the marker regime declares nothing, which the census line makes visible. Second, every item runs with a **private `TMPDIR`** created under the run directory and removed when the item finishes -- so a harness's view of its temp directory is the view it has when run alone, and peak temp usage is bounded by the worker count rather than by the corpus. `TMPDIR` is the only environment variable this runner sets for a harness. **BTG-143 (one recorded stderr-only change; one additive stdout line; the verdict is untouched):** the per-tree dispatch queue is now a **stable solo-first partition** of the same byte-wise sorted union -- the declared real-tree writers above, in union order, then everything else, in union order -- and it is that shape at **every worker count**, unconditionally. The reason it is unconditional rather than applied only above one worker is this row's own `--workers 1` promise: a dispatch order that differed by worker count would make that bisect change **two** variables at once, so unconditional ordering keeps it a genuine one-variable control and additionally makes `--workers 1` reproduce the W=8 **order** as well as its one-at-a-time execution. *Whether* a declared writer runs alone is unchanged -- the drain, the exclusive-window latch and the `runs ALONE` announcement are byte-unchanged; only *when* it runs changed, so the pool is already empty when the first one is dispatched and the drain stalls that cost a measured ~1042 s of a 2790 s sweep are not incurred. **Changed on stderr only:** the order of the `RUNNING` progress lines and the position of the `runs ALONE` announcements. The stdout report is unaffected because it iterates the sorted union rather than dispatch or completion order. **Added on stdout:** for each `FIXED` row that nothing explains, one additive `FIXED-ADVISORY <harness> ...` line naming the exact `--workers 1` re-run command -- a **new** line with its own prefix, emitted after every pre-existing block, so no existing row's bytes move (the BTG-135 `SCEN-` precedent). It is **advisory only and does NOT change the verdict**: `FIXED` remains outside the failing fold and the exit-code vocabulary is unchanged. It fires iff **all five** hold -- the class is `FIXED`; workers > 1 (so the advisory is structurally silent in the very run it recommends, which is also its off switch); the harness is **not** in the solo set; the harness file is **byte-identical** on both trees; and **no repository-relative path the harness names differs between the trees**. The last condition is the discriminating one: byte-identity alone is necessary but **not** sufficient, because a legitimate `FIXED` means the branch fixed the *code under test*, which leaves the harness byte-identical too -- a one-condition rule would fire on the normal case and train the operator to ignore it. **Its residual class is two-sided, and is stated here as shipped behaviour (BTG-143 decisions.md DEC-016, which corrects both the figures and the false-negative category that DEC-015 first recorded here):** that last condition screens what a harness **mentions**, not what it **depends on**, so it is wrong in both directions. **False negative -- the silent direction, and it is a matter of GRANULARITY, not of incidental prose:** the screen is **file-granular**, so a harness that reads a file in order to assert on **one row** of it is suppressed by a diff to **any other row** of that same file. Measured on the BTG-143 branch over the 130-harness corpus, 51 harnesses were suppressed and **41 of those 51 solely by this registry file** (`docs/policies/claire-surfaces.md`) -- a file every Medium+ ticket is **required** to edit, so the workflow's single most common edit unscreens **41 of 130 harnesses (31.5%)** while the operator sees exactly the silence a clean screen produces (the same epistemic state `baseline.fixed.advisory_unavailable` announces, reached with **no** announcement). Stated in the honest direction, because it bounds how much of that 31.5% is actually a blind spot: for **38** of those 41 this registry is a **genuine dependency they read** -- assigned to a variable and grepped -- so their suppression is condition 5 **working as designed**, merely coarsened to whole-file granularity; only **3** (`btg-095-live-verification-governance.test.sh`, `btg-132-registered-surface-fixes.test.sh`, `pi-057-verify-spec-facet-loop.test.sh`) cite it in a **comment alone**, making the genuinely-incidental class **3 of 130 -- 2.3%**. **False positive:** a path assembled with an interpolated (`$VAR`) segment is invisible to extraction -- only its literal prefix survives, and a bare directory is discarded -- so a harness whose real dependency is named that way screens as naming nothing and gets an advisory it does not deserve; 43 of those 130 carry such a path (a globbed segment is the same mechanism and is not counted in that 43). A **transitive** dependency -- reaching changed code only through an intermediary it does not name -- is a further case of that same direction. None of this touches the verdict, which is why it is recorded rather than fixed; a sound fix is a dependency analysis, deferred as OQ-6(b)'s follow-on with those figures as its baseline, each reproducible by the exact command recorded in DEC-016. Seams added on stderr: `SEAM_VIOLATION baseline.fixed.unexplained` (the advisory itself) and `SEAM_VIOLATION baseline.fixed.advisory_unavailable` (the screen could not be computed -- announced, never silently resolved in either direction, the same idiom `baseline.tree.immutability_guard_unavailable` uses). The 38/3 split is measured by a single reproducible discriminator -- **whether the token appears on a line outside a comment** -- not by an assessment of whether the harness genuinely consumes the file; under a stricter "does it read the file's content" reading, two of the 38 are fixture-tree cases and the genuinely-incidental class is 4 of 130 (3.1%) rather than 3 (2.3%). A **globbed** path segment is the same extraction failure as an interpolated one and is **not counted** in the 43. **Consumer note on the prefix:** the advisory line begins with the bytes `FIXED-ADVISORY`, so a consumer anchoring on `^FIXED` **without a delimiter** will count advisory lines as `FIXED` rows; `^FIXED ` (with a trailing space) matches genuine rows only, since the class token is padded to 9 characters. No existing row's bytes moved. All eighteen real-tree write sites were relocated into `mktemp`-rooted scratch trees and every declaration marker removed, so the per-run census line reads `baseline-diff: solo set = none` and the drain-and-`runs ALONE` mechanism retains no subject. The seven formerly-solo harnesses may therefore now emit advisory lines they previously could not. The advisory is stderr-only and the verdict is untouched, so no consumer contract changes. **The residual, stated honestly:** a census of `none` and a guard reporting `0 declared exemption(s)` prove the corpus carries no *detectable* write into the repository tree -- **not that it carries none**. The guard resolves a write destination one hop, so a destination assembled across two or more hops is invisible to it; four such sites existed and were found by a during-run observer rather than by any static scan (BTG-142 decisions.md DEC-011/DEC-013). Do not read the empty census as a proof of absence. Pinned by `ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-138-tree-immutability.test.sh` (glob-derived, zero unexempted sites) and `btg-143-solo-first.test.sh` S-1.8, whose non-vacuity precondition was re-expressed as a corpus-ranged check when this ticket emptied the set (DEC-014, ratified at the maintainer gate). **BTG-148 (citation only -- no behaviour, grammar, contract or consumer change):** the four-mechanism scratch-tree relocation taxonomy those eighteen sites used (M1 / M2 / M2-cwd / M3), the execute-the-callee procedure for selecting between its members, and the one-hop residual stated immediately above are recorded as a standing decision in ADR_CLAIRE-0060 (`docs/ADR/0060-a-scratch-tree-relocation-mechanism-is-chosen-by-executing-the-callee-never-by-reading-it.md`). **BTG-192 (a fourth classification, and the first verdict relaxation on this surface):** a newly-red SCENARIO may now fold `SCEN-CONTENDED`, and its harness `CONTENDED`, instead of `NEW-RED`. Both tokens are appended to their counts lines (`CONTENDED` ninth on the harness line, seventh on the `scenarios:` line), so fields 1..8 and 1..6 do not move and a positional parser is unaffected; only a field-COUNT parser sees a change. `CONTENDED` is exactly nine characters and `SCEN-CONTENDED` exactly fourteen, so they fit the existing `%-9s` and `%-14s` row pads and no column shifts. **`CONTENDED` sits OUTSIDE the failing fold** -- a run that previously reported `VERDICT FAIL` and exited 1 may now report `VERDICT PASS` and exit 0. It is earned by four conditions, never by a duration: (1) an in-source marker `wall-clock-ceiling BTG-192 scenario=<id> adapter=<name>` in the scenario's own harness, glob-derived across both trees and never a roster, whose grammar is closed -- both fields required and non-empty, and `<name>` must name an adapter that tree's compiler carries; (2) `WORKERS > 1`, so `--workers 1` is structurally unable to disposition anything and remains the manual bisect; (3) the **declaring harness file itself** byte-identical on both trees once its declaration lines are stripped -- `ci-templates/scripts/tests/` sits OUTSIDE the compile-input closure condition 4 screens, so without this a branch could edit the very scenario body its own marker vouches for and still be dispositioned; a difference REFUSES and announces `baseline.timing.screen_refused` naming the harness, while a marker present on one tree only is still admitted; and (4) the compile-input digest, from the new unregistered `claire-compile.sh --input-digest` mode, byte-equal on both trees. Six new stderr seams, all advisory to the reader and none verdict-changing except through the fold above: `baseline.timing.contended` (a disposition, with its harness, scenario, adapter, compared digest and a single-worker re-run command), `baseline.timing.screen_refused` (digests differ; disposition withheld), `baseline.timing.screen_unavailable` (uncomputable; emitted at most once per adapter per run), `baseline.timing.marker_ungrammatical` (a near-miss marker, refused rather than coerced), `baseline.timing.census_unresolvable` (a tree whose harness directory could not be read, so no absence in the set is evidence) and `baseline.timing.disposition_rate` (a provisional drift band, or a declaration new on the branch under test). A `baseline-diff: timing set = ...` census line is announced on stderr on EVERY run -- sorted, and `none` when nothing is declared -- so the mechanism's membership is visible rather than latent. A harness is dispositioned only when EVERY one of its newly-red scenarios was individually dispositioned and at least one was, so an undeclared newly-red scenario keeps the whole harness red. Hosted in a seventh runner module, `ci-templates/scripts/baseline-contention.sh`, which also now hosts BTG-143's FIXED-row advisory, relocated there verbatim and behaviourally unchanged. Stability and guarantee period are UNCHANGED. **BTG-298 (the disposable-copy guarantee strengthens from working-tree content to content plus a private git store, in every topology; the per-item `TMPDIR` clause moves to a separate root; one additive stdout line; one additive-but-stricter verdict term):** after the content copy, the copy's `.git` (pointer file or directory -- one code path serves both topologies) is now discarded and replaced by a store **private to the copy**, materialised by `git clone --local --no-hardlinks --no-checkout --dissociate` from the origin's `--git-common-dir`, with the origin's index copied in and `HEAD` detached at the origin's commit; a post-condition probe HALTs (`IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.branchcopy.store_not_private`, exit 2, before any harness runs) if the severed copy still resolves `--git-common-dir` outward, and any failure to materialise the private store HALTs the same way (`baseline.branchcopy.sever_failed`). `--dissociate` (code review cycle 2, BLOCKING 2) closes an alternates-file reachability gap the `--git-common-dir` probe alone cannot see: without it, an origin itself built with `--reference`/`--shared` yields a copy whose object store still resolves outside the copy even though the probe passes. **Additive-but-stricter refusal (code review cycle 2, BLOCKING 3; `sequencer/` marker added code review cycle 3, BLOCKING 2):** the run also HALTs (`IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.branchcopy.origin_in_progress`, exit 2, before any harness runs) if the origin carries an in-progress git operation (merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, bisect, including the sequencer/-only window after a conflicted multi-commit cherry-pick or revert commits a resolved step) -- an operator running the sweep mid-merge or mid-rebase now gets this HALT where the surface previously severed and swept silently. A genuinely absent origin index (e.g. one removed out from under the origin, or a `--no-checkout` clone used as an origin) is announced rather than silenced (`LINEAGE_GAP baseline.branchcopy.no_origin_index`), never treated as a fallback success. This closes the reachability BTG-292 DEC-041 recorded and deferred: three prior destructions of the operator's own `.git` / `.claude/` / `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes`, all in worktree topology, where a `cp -a` copy's `.git` was a `gitdir:` pointer resolving to the ORIGINAL's store. A no-op, cost zero, when the tree under test is not a git work tree. Every reader this runner has (dirty-status resolution, the tree fingerprint, the comparison-ref lookup, BTG-143's screen) sees the severed copy's store, verified byte-identical to the origin's (`git status --porcelain`, `HEAD`, the resolving comparison ref, staged-but-uncommitted blobs) -- this is a REAL behavioural change for any harness that itself resolves `--git-common-dir` or otherwise reads git state at run time, named rather than asserted away (`ADR_CLAIRE-0109`, amending `ADR_CLAIRE-0058`'s narrower per-worker-copy rejection). **The per-item `TMPDIR`** this row already documents as "created under the run directory" now lives under a SEPARATE scratch root, its own `mktemp` template sharing no prefix with the run directory's, so a harness deleting near its own temp area cannot take the run's log/result trees with it; the row's existing per-item-directory guarantee (private, removed at item end) is unchanged, only its parent moved -- announced on a new `baseline-diff: scratch = ...` header line immediately after the pre-existing `logs = ...` line. Roots that are not disjoint HALT at second zero (`baseline.scratch.shared_root`). **If the run's own log/result tree is lost mid-sweep** (the run directory or its log subtree disappears, becomes unwritable, or the filesystem fills or exhausts inodes) the FIRST such failure is classified by name (absent / not-a-directory / not-writable / filesystem-full / inodes-exhausted / unknown), emitted as exactly one `IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.rundir.lost` naming the classification, the item ordinal and the in-flight set with ages -- replacing what was previously an unattributed cascade of per-item `LINEAGE_GAP baseline.log.unwritable` rows with no diagnosis and no printed verdict. Recovery is attempted exactly once (in place, else at a fresh run directory) and announced (`SEAM_VIOLATION baseline.rundir.recovered`, or `IMPOSSIBLE_STATE baseline.rundir.unrecoverable` if both fail); the pre-existing per-item `ERROR` fold for the affected item(s) is unchanged and additive. One new stdout line, its own prefix, after every pre-existing block: `EVIDENCE-LOSS <classification> first at item <n>/<N> on the <label> tree; recovered at <path>` -- no existing row's bytes move. **Additive-but-stricter:** a run that diagnosed a loss can never exit 0 (`RUNDIR_LOST` joins `CONTAMINATED` in the fail-closed fold), over a state in which the tool previously could not print a verdict at all. Per-item scratch is retained (not removed) from the moment a loss is diagnosed, announced once (`LINEAGE_GAP baseline.scratch.retained`); a healthy run removes the scratch root entirely, unchanged from today's per-item cleanup in the normal case. No new dependency: `git`, `mktemp`, `cp`, `rm`, `df` are all already required or already carried in the harness's own tool list. Measured added cost: one local clone (~0.14 s) against a 644 s reference sweep (~0.02%); no per-item or between-dispatch probing in the steady state. Hosted in an eighth runner module, `ci-templates/scripts/baseline-runroot.sh` (run-root lifecycle, moved out of `baseline-diff.sh`'s entry point verbatim); severing lives in `baseline-branch-copy.sh`. New Beta surface registered: the managed-block marker contract (see row below). **BTG-132 (internal decomposition, behavior-preserving):** the entry point breached the PI-037 400-line DX ceiling at 506 lines and was split along a NAMED behavioral seam -- **copy / provision**. `adopt-claire.sh` (now 257) copies framework-owned bytes; a new co-located module **`adopt-provision.sh`** (307) provisions what the ADOPTER owns: the repository skeleton (`CHANGELOG.md`, `archive/`, `specs/drafts/`), the generated create-once artifacts (`footprint.generated`, the dead-citation baseline, `.claire-version`), the surgical registrations into `settings.json` / `.mcp.json`, and the PI-039 id-ledger seed. **No new registered surface:** the module is internal, sourced-never-executed, and not independently invocable -- the same status `gitignore-block.sh` holds, and it carries no `manifest.generated` row (the manifest names one `sidecar=` per command). It travels by the existing whole-sidecar-dir copy (II-016) to fresh adopters and by the `kind=tree_root identity=commands` union to already-adopted repos, so **no adopter action and no `RECONCILE` row** is required. The invocation contract, flags, exit codes, output ordering and resulting tree are UNCHANGED, verified by a real end-to-end adoption diffed against a baseline captured on the unsplit tree -- byte-identical but for the delivery of the new module itself (`specs/BTG-132/decisions.md` DEC-005/DEC-016). **BTG-198 (modification; additive from the adopter's perspective):** `CLAUDE.md` **leaves `COPY_PATHS`** and is no longer copied verbatim — it is GENERATED, and is categorically adopter-owned (`kind=seed`). The shipped directives move to a new framework-owned root file `CLAIRE_DIRECTIVES.md`, which enters `COPY_PATHS`. Adoption is **always-sidecar**: ONE code path regardless of whether the target arrived with a `CLAUDE.md`. No target → a generated adopter-owned stub whose FIRST line is the sidecar import; existing `CLAUDE.md` → a marker-fenced managed block appended at EOF, every byte outside it preserved, replaced (never duplicated) on re-adopt. The previous behaviour — a bare `skip (exists): CLAUDE.md` leaving the adopter with ZERO CLAIRE directives — was a **defect, not a guarantee**, so the observable contract is not broken: an adopter still ends a run with the directives installed. New in the run: an unconditional post-adopt assertion (`LINEAGE_GAP adopt.context.sidecar_missing` / `adopt.context.block_missing`) that refuses a false success, an `IMPOSSIBLE_STATE adopt.context.target_not_writable` / `adopt.context.unterminated_block` refusal that leaves the file byte-untouched, a `DECISION_DRIFT adopt.context.block_action` seam reporting `stub`/`written`/`replaced`, and a one-per-run conflict-review NOTICE on stdout stating that the adopter's own directives may conflict with CLAIRE behaviors and that a human resolves them. Under `--gitignore-machinery` BOTH context files are carved out of the managed ignore block (DEC-011) — ignoring half the wiring would leave a fresh clone importing a file that is not in the remote. **BTG-314 (behavior correction, not a break -- OQ-8 (a)):** adopt gains a release phase that runs before any byte reaches `$DST`: resolves the release commit via the same tag-bounded `core_commit_for_version` `/claire-upgrade` uses (sourced from `artifacts/commands/claire-upgrade/upgrade-resolve.sh` in the running checkout), materializes that commit's own tree with an archive of its objects, writes the stamp, then hands the copy/provision work to **that tree's own adopt engine** via a private cross-version handshake (`CLAIRE_ADOPT_RELEASE_TREE`, refused loud outside a materialized tree -- never an adopter-facing flag). The installed bytes, the eject descriptor, the hook/MCP registrations and the id-ledger seed therefore all come from the one commit `commit=` names; the checkout's working tree (including any unreleased local work) is never installed. A core checkout with no version-control metadata now aborts before any write instead of writing an empty `commit=`. Re-adopt installs the **stamp's** commit, not a newer one in the checkout; if that commit is absent from the checkout, adopt announces `DRIFT_SIGNAL adopt.release_tree.stamp_commit_unavailable` and falls back to a fresh resolution, leaving the stamp untouched. See `specs/BTG-314/spec.md`. |

The writer matches the first open-marker → first-close-marker region (idempotency). Changing either marker line text **orphans existing blocks** (re-run appends a duplicate instead of replacing). The block content (the path list) is derived from `artifacts/footprint.generated` at write time and may change across core versions; only the marker text is the stability contract. The `>>>` / `<<<` shape mirrors the existing `>>> binding-resolution <<<` fence convention. An **unterminated** block (open marker present, close marker absent — externally corrupted) is **refused loudly** with the file left byte-untouched rather than silently truncated (DEC-016). |

## Ruled not registered

**Added by BTG-275 under Gate 1's OQ-3 ruling. Additive: no existing row, table or
stability vocabulary above changes.** This table exists because **an empty or silent
registry is never evidence** (`change-tiers.md`, *Empty is never evidence*). Before it,
a surface with no row was ambiguous between *ruled not registered*, *overlooked* and
*registered elsewhere by a glob* -- and the next triager re-derived the answer from
first principles, which is the cost five folded tickets were filed to end. A ruling is
recorded in **either** direction; "no row" is never the answer.

**A row here grants nothing and withdraws nothing.** It records that a surface is not
registered and *why*, so the absence becomes evidence. Everything here remains covered
by `CLAIRE_ORG.md` section 3 Facet 5's **second** activation limb ("or any
adopter-facing contract") where it is adopter-facing, which is the obligation that
applied before this table existed and applies unchanged after it.

**The reason is the load-bearing column.** A reason that restates the absence ("it is
not listed") is circular and is rejected by
`ci-templates/scripts/tests/btg-275-registry-completeness.test.sh`, which also fails if
any corpus item -- every `/`-command, every role, every numbered `CLAIRE_ORG.md`
section, every `docs/policies/` document and every `specs/TEMPLATE/` file, all DERIVED
from the tree rather than listed here -- carries no ruling at all.

**The org-section class predicate**, ruled at BTG-275's Gate 1 (OQ-1) and **amended at that
ticket's code-review gate to add its second limb** (BTG-275 DEC-016). Applied to every
`CLAIRE_ORG.md` row below and above:

> A section is a registered surface **iff** it is a per-adopter-substituted contract that at least one
> CLAIRE tool or role resolves **as a value**, **AND** is declared as a **contract** rather than as a
> **practice**.

It **admits** sections 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 19, each of which carries a row in
*Configuration Contracts* above, and **excludes** the nine below. It is a **class** ruling: a section
is dispositioned by the predicate, never by a one-off judgment about that section.

**Both limbs are load-bearing, and the second one earns its place on a measured counter-example.** As
first ruled the predicate had only the first limb, and section 16 satisfied it:
`ci-templates/scripts/authored-doc-orgtoken.sh` derives its token set from that section's
`**Target - always X, by name.**` clauses, which is resolution as a value. The first limb therefore
**admitted a section the ruling's own enumeration excluded**, and the enumeration had to be followed
*over* the predicate's wording -- a class rule that cannot decide its own hardest case. The second
limb decides it: section 16 declares of itself that it is **NOT a binding**, so it is a practice
record and the limb excludes it. Predicate and enumeration now agree, and no section is dispositioned
by anything other than the rule.

Two further predicates were put to the gate and **rejected** -- *the anchor name ends in `-binding`*
(falsified by `CLAIRE_ORG.md#model-tier-mapping`, a plain numbered section that carries a row) and
*an adopter substitutes it* (over-inclusive: it admits section 1).

consults, and BTG-275 settles the underlying ambiguity: Gate 1 (OQ-2) ruled that

## OpenCode-adapter harness known-red set (BTG-054)

The OpenCode-adapter BDD harness (`ci-templates/scripts/tests/opencode-adapter.test.sh`) is a
first-class **blocking** `run-gates.sh` row (see the `run-gates.sh` cell above). Its known-red
disposition, reconciled by BTG-054:

- **The known-red set is empty.** All four scenarios that were baseline-red on `origin/main`
  independent of any single ticket — **S-7.2** (committed `.claude/` golden byte-identical),
  **S-3.3** (emitted `.opencode/*.md` frontmatter/body load-check), **S-10.1** (fenced upgrade
  sidecars pass the sweep), **S-10.3** (OpenCode-emitted upgrade engine stays Claude-coupled) —
  were **fixed by assertion-correction**, not registered as accepted-known-red. Each was a stale or
  mis-scoped *test assertion* that drifted as the surrounding code evolved (the compiler, the
  `opencode.sh` adapter, the upgrade sidecars, and the golden fixture were all correct and are
  byte-unchanged). Fail-injection guards (S-1.5/S-1.6/S-1.7) prove each corrected assertion still
  fails closed on a genuine regression.
- **The harness is now a blocking `run-gates.sh` row.** A green-and-gated baseline means any future
  red is unambiguously a **regression** (a reviewer no longer re-derives "is this pre-existing
  baseline-red?" from a fresh baseline diff); a red harness fails the composed merge verdict and
  cannot silently pass. Re-entrancy is bounded by the `CLAIRE_GATES_RUNNING` sentinel.
- **The S-10.3 Claude-coupling remains a documented known gap, deferred to PI-028 — pinned green,
  not accepted-red.** The OpenCode-emitted upgrade engine stays Claude-coupled (the hook-expansion
  path in the emitted `upgrade-collect.sh` sources `adapters/claude-code.sh` and calls
  `cc_expand_body`). S-10.3 asserts that coupling is **present** (a correct green test), so it will
  go red only when PI-028 actually decouples the upgrade engine. This is a documented gap, not a
  test defect and not an accepted baseline-red.
